title: Broccoli Cheddar Soup
subtitle: Panera-style — thick, velvety and loaded with old cheddar
imageAlt: Bowl of broccoli cheddar soup with shredded cheddar and a slice of crusty bread
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2–3 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Shred the cheddar from a block — pre-shredded can make the soup grainy.
Chop the broccoli small (bite-size florets, peeled stems diced) so every spoonful gets some.
Use a big pot or Dutch oven (at least 4 L).

items.name: broccoli
items.note: small florets + peeled stems, diced (~6 cups)

items.name: ground nutmeg
items.note: just a pinch — it makes it taste like Panera's

items.name: shredded old cheddar
items.note: freshly shredded, plus extra to top

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Melt the butter in a big pot over medium. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and cook 4–5 minutes until soft and see-through, not browned. Add the garlic for the last minute.

steps.title: Make the roux
steps.text: Sprinkle in the flour and stir constantly 1–2 minutes so it loses its raw taste.

steps.title: Add the liquids
steps.text: Slowly whisk in the broth, then the half-and-half, until smooth. Bring to a gentle simmer (don't boil hard).

steps.title: Simmer the veg
steps.text: Add the broccoli, carrots, salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and nutmeg. Simmer on medium-low, partly covered and stirring often, 15–20 minutes until the broccoli is very tender.

steps.title: Make it velvety
steps.text: For that Panera texture, blend about a third of the soup with an immersion blender (or blend 2 cups in a blender, vented, and stir back in). Leave plenty of chunks.

steps.title: Melt in the cheddar
steps.text: Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until melted and smooth, saving a small handful for the top. Taste and add salt until it's well seasoned. Serve topped with the saved cheddar and crusty bread.

fixIt.fix: The cheese went in while it was too hot, or it was pre-shredded. Always add cheese off the heat, a handful at a time.
Simmer uncovered 5 minutes, or blend a bit more of the soup. Extra cheddar thickens it too.
Stir in broth or milk, ¼ cup at a time. It thickens a lot overnight.
Add salt ¼ tsp at a time — cheese soups need it. A pinch more nutmeg or garlic powder helps.

saleTip: Broccoli crowns are often 2 for $4–5 at No Frills, and old cheddar 400 g blocks hit ~$5–6 on sale — use the leftover 100 g on tacos or mac and cheese.
swap: Use whole milk instead of half-and-half (a little lighter), or frozen broccoli (no need to thaw; simmer 10–12 min).
leftovers: Fridge 4 days. Reheat on low, stirring, with a splash of milk — don't boil or it can split. Freezing isn't recommended (the cheese turns grainy).
doneness: Broccoli stems are tender when pierced. Keep it below a boil once the cheese is in, or it turns grainy. Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested Panera-copycat broccoli cheddar soup methods (Once Upon a Chef, Food Network Kitchen): butter-flour roux, broth + half-and-half, partial blend, cheese off the heat.
gear: Large pot or Dutch oven (4 L+)
prepAhead: Chop the broccoli, grate the carrots and dice the onion up to 2 days ahead; store in containers in the fridge.
Shred the cheddar ahead and keep it in a sealed bag.
reheat: Low heat on the stove, stirring often, with a splash of milk until steaming — never boil or the cheese can split. Microwave at 50% power, 1 min at a time, stirring.

basic.note: Broccoli, broth, milk and cheddar — creamy without the extras.

stepNotes.3: Basic: broccoli, salt, pepper and garlic powder.

fancy.note: Velvety Panera-style soup in a crusty bread bowl with crispy cheddar frico and toasted broccoli tips.

1-0.name: small crusty rounds or bread bowls

stepNotes.3: Fancy: hold back a handful of small florets, roast them at 220°C (425°F) for 10 minutes for the top.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Bake small mounds of cheddar on parchment at 200°C (400°F) for 6–8 minutes until lacy and golden; cool to crisp. Hollow the bread rounds, toast them 5 minutes, ladle in the soup and top with roasted florets and a cheddar crisp.

plating: Toast the bread bowl first so it doesn't go soggy.
Fill just below the rim and stand a cheddar crisp in the soup.
Three roasted florets on top, not more.

why.0-3: Flour makes the roux that keeps the cheese smooth. Without it the soup is thin and can turn grainy.
why.0-12: A pinch of nutmeg is the Panera secret. Leave it out and it's just a little plainer.
why.0-13: Freshly shredded cheddar melts smoothly; bagged has starch that can make it gritty.

funFact: Cheddar is named after the village of Cheddar in Somerset, England, where cheese was once aged in the cool caves of Cheddar Gorge.

keeps.note: the cheese sauce goes grainy once frozen

pairs: Soup and sandwich night — make the Philly while the soup simmers
